title: Scale economies: embeddings pricing playbook and contract checklist
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Enterprise customers and embedding-heavy products (semantic search, personalization, reranking) are pushing token and vector volumes far beyond our single-request pricing model. We need a defensible, easy-to-explain pricing playbook that: (1) transitions to per-vector economics in a way that preserves revenue, (2) offers volume/batch incentives to encourage efficient bulk calls, and (3) maps cleanly to enterprise contracts / QSA requirements.

Goals: Provide a recommended pricing ladder and negotiation guidance for sales; run an internal pilot with select customers for batch-discount tiers; prepare artifacts for QSA and procurement teams (sample contract language, SPIFFs, and security/compliance checklist).

Success metrics: 1) Reduction in effective cost per vector for customers at >10M vectors/month while maintaining or increasing revenue per customer; 2) Adoption of batch endpoints by 30% of heavy customers within 90 days of rollout; 3) Legal/QSA signoff on contract language and data handling checklist without major redlines.

Hypothesis: Introducing a per-vector unit with explicit batch-discounted tiers (bucketed by monthly volume and single-call batch size) will increase committed spend from large customers and reduce inefficient one-off calls to the non-bundled API.

Experiment design: 1) Define 3-tier ladder: Starter (<1M vectors/mo), Growth (1M-50M), Enterprise (>50M) with effective per-vector rates and minimum monthly commitments for Growth/Enterprise. 2) Offer a behavioral discount for using the batched endpoint: +10% effective discount for average batch size >=64 vectors, +20% for >=256. 3) Run a 90-day pilot with 6 existing large customers (mix of AI-native and enterprise) — two negotiated discounted pilots, two opt-in standard tiers, two observational (no change) to measure behavioral shift. 4) Instrument billing and Console metrics: per-customer vector volume, batch size distribution, latency impact, and revenue per vector.

Contract/QSA checklist deliverables: sample SOW language for committed volumes, data isolation and retention terms, acceptable use and reprocessing clauses, audit log requirements, KMS/HSM integration references, and a minimal required response to a QSA questionnaire showing how batch processing affects data flow and access control.

Competitive considerations: Other providers advertise simple per-embedding pricing; we must keep simplicity in customer-facing docs but preserve negotiation flexibility for enterprise (reserved capacity + batch incentives).

Risks & trade-offs: Complex tiering may confuse self-serve users — mitigate with clear Console cost calculator. Large batch incentives could encourage customers to trade latency for cost — enforce SLO notes and recommend dedicated pools for heavy batch workloads. Revenue risk from aggressive entry discounts — cap pilots and require finance signoff on minimum commitments.

Deliverables: pricing playbook doc for sales, legal contract language snippets, QSA-ready checklist packet, pilot instrumentation dashboard, and post-pilot readout with recommendation to general availability or iterate.

Links and artifacts: Confluence playbook (placeholder: https://confluence.internal/redwood/embeddings-pricing-playbook), sample contract PRD (https://drive.google.com/sample-contract), pilot onboarding checklist (https://docs.redwood/pilot-onboard), billing dashboard mock (https://grafana.redwood/embeddings-billing).

notes_for_finance_and_sales: Propose baseline per-vector list price: $0.0012/vector (Starter); Growth effective range $0.0009-$0.0006 depending on commitment; Enterprise negotiated below $0.0005 with minimum monthly commitment.
Batch incentives should be modeled as effective discounts rather than separate SKUs to keep invoicing simple.
Require minimum 3-month ramp commit for pilot discounts and finance approval for any trial giving >20% effective discount.
Offer an add-on for 'burst compute' to cover unexpected spike cost if customer uses batched runs beyond reserved capacity.
